title: EGY-04 · The past and denial but...-š

blocks.text: EGY-04 · The past and denial but...-š
Lesson overview

With EGY present-03 tell your habits; with the past tell what happened: the weekend, the trip, yesterday's day. The Egyptian past is the perfect of fuṣḥā Without cases and with a little different vowels: katab, katabt, katabit. Denial surrounds the verb: ma-katabtiš I didn't write it. Study also the most frequent irregular verbs (ruḥt, šuft, ʾult, gēt), the expressions of past and smooth time just / not yet. Six weeks, in parallel with B1-09, B1-10 and B1-11.

rows: 8–9 hours · six weeks (weeks 113–118), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or Egyptian conversation partner, tutor recordings on the phone
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. to combine regular verbs and the most common irregular verbs in the past;
2. To deny the past with but...-š, even with the pronouns attacked;
3. place a fact in time (imbāriḥ, il-usbūʿ ili fātmin yomēn);
4. use lysa and lysa but...-š Not yet ʿumri ma- ... never;
5. tell what you did and ask others what they did.
Six-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).
1. Dialogue 1 · The weekend
Tuesday, tandem at the Polytechnic bar.

2. The Egyptian past and the fuṣḥā

rows: no final vowel: you and I are the same
many verbs have instead of a in the first syllable

blocks.text: ana and inta have the same shape (katabt). The context or pronoun decide: an katabt / inta katabt.
3. Conjugation

The vowel that falls. In verbs in (i)širib, fihim), in front of -it and -u the second i falls: širbit, širbu, fihmu. Four-letter verbs (from derived forms): ištaġalt, ištaġal, ištaġalit, ištaġalu; zākirt, zākir, zakrit, zakru; Itkallimt, itkallim, itkallimit, itkallimu.
4. The most frequent irregular verbs
ištara Buying ištarēt ištarēti ištara ištarit ištarēna ištaru

The guys. 1. Concave verbs (rāḥ, šāf, ʾāl, nām): long vowel with people without consonant suffix (rāḥ, rāḥit, rāḥu), short with the others (ruḥt, ruḥna). 2. Verbs ending in vowel (miši, ištara, ṣiḥi Wake up: in front of the consonant suffix appears ē or ī (ištarēt, ṣiḥīt). 3. kal and ḫad: the hamza of fuṣḥā ( ⁧أَكَلَ⁩ , ⁧أَخَذَ⁩ ) is gone.
5. Denial but...-š

rows: did not write · I did not go
I didn't see it. I didn't see it.

blocks.text: The vowel before -š. The -š wants a long syllable in front: katabt → ma-katabtiš (add i), katabu → ma- katabūš (the u stretches), katabti → ma-katabtīš. miš with the past is used only for a strong contrast or in a rhetorical question: miš ʾultillak? Didn't I tell you?
6. Setting up in time

rows: iš-šahr ili fāt · is-sana lli fātit
two days ago · one month ago

blocks.text: once · twice marra · marritēn

min with the past is valid wṣilt min sāʿa I arrived an hour ago. The following shall be added: baštaġal hina min sana \\work here for one year. kān + present for past habits (you saw it in EGY-03): kunt baṣḥa mitʾaḫḫar I woke up late, kānit bitrūḥ il-madrasa māšya He went to school on foot.

8. lissa, ḫalāṣ, ʿumri

rows: lissa ma-kaltiš I haven't eaten yet.
Kalt? - It's smooth. Have you eaten? Not yet.
ʿumri ma-ruḥt Aswān I've never been to Aswan

blocks.text: 9. Pronunciation

The -it of the female. katabit, rāḥit, ʾālit: one brief clear, not the a fuṣḥā. The -š that stretches. ma-ruḥtiš, ma-šuftūš, ma-kaltīš: the accent falls on the long syllable before -š. Repeat after tutor: ma-ruḥtiš / ma-ruḥtīš (f.). Shadowing. The tutor reads the dialog 2 with the tone of a worried mother; You repeat the lines of Šarīf, then those of Umm Šarīf.
10. New lexicon

rows: nizilt is-sūʾ I went to the market.
awwil imbāriḥ The day before yesterday

blocks.text: Notes.ṭiliʿ and nizil are wild verbs: ṭiliʿ il-ʾahwa He climbed to the bar and also ṭiliʿ min il-bēt He's out of the house. ṭiliʿ dukṭūr He has become a doctor. nizil ... is down, but also out (in town) ... ʿamal be done in almost all senses: ʿamal ʾahwa "He made coffee" ʿamal ḥādsa He had an accident.

Exercise 7 · What have they done?
Listen to Script B and write for each person three things he has done and one that he has not done.
12. Listening
Egyptian scripts should be read by an Egyptian speaker (tutor, tandem partner): vocal synthesis does not pronounce the dialect reliably.
Script A · Dialogues 1 and 2
The reader reads the dialogues at normal speed. Listen without reading, then answer questions a) and b) for the year 8.
Script B · Yesterday

⁧صحابي في كافيه. بس ما ذاكرتش خالص، علشان كنت تعبانة.⁩

How was your test? b) Dialogue 2: Why is the mother worried? What he ate Šarīf And how does the mother react? What he doesn't know yet Šarīf? What he complains about Yāsmīn? 13. Oral production
1. My weekend (session). Tell the tutor your last weekend in two minutes; the tutor makes you questions (ruḥt fēn? maʿa mīn? ʿamaltu ēh? rigiʿt ).
2. Mom's interview. Role-playing game: The tutor makes the Egyptian mother worried (kalt? Nimt? ʿamalt il-imtiḥān?); You answer, even with denials and laxity.
3. Never and not yet. Ask the tutor five questions with ʿumrak… ʾabl Kida? And answer yours.

17. To switch to the next unit

Switch to EGY-05 if you have at least 16/20 and if you told your weekend to the tutor (oral production 1) using at least eight verbs in the past and two negations. In EGY-05 learn the future with ḥa- and make plans, invitations and appointments.
